summary:
MUZAREE is an interactive decision-support web platform that transforms 36 years of NASA Earth Observation data into simple, reliable multi-year crop rotation plans. Using a 3D MapLibre GL satellite globe marked with 12 NASA data-collection regions across the US Great Plains and Midwest, farmers draw their field boundary, select wheat, and receive three tailored 2- to 4-year plans: an Existing Rotation baseline, a Water-Efficient plan, and a Soil-Building plan, plus a side-by-side comparison table.

Behind the interface sits a two-layer scientific engine: a 400-tree gradient-boosting model (HistGradientBoostingRegressor) trained on 32,967 records and 68 NASA POWER climate, SMAP soil-moisture, and soil-profile features (achieving 0.952 R² and ±0.388 t/ha MAE on unseen 2009–2016 years), paired with an agronomic optimizer evaluating 24 valid wheat-inclusive rotations and transparent reliability checks.

Continuous monoculture degrades soil health and strains water supplies, yet raw satellite datasets remain hard for farmers to interpret. MUZAREE bridges this gap, turning spaceborne data into clear, trustworthy guidance that conserves water, restores soil, and supports resilient harvests.
details:
1. What does it do & how does it work?

MUZAREE turns 36 years of NASA Earth Observation data (1981–2016) into multi-year crop rotation plans. On a 3D satellite globe marked with 12 NASA data regions (US Great Plains & Midwest), farmers draw their field, select Wheat, and view three 2–4 year plans—Existing, Water-Efficient, and Soil-Building—plus a comparison table. A 400-tree ML model (HistGradientBoostingRegressor) trained on 68 NASA POWER weather, SMAP moisture, and soil features predicts yield (t/ha), while an optimizer scores 24 valid rotations.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact:

Makes spaceborne data practical for farmers, helping conserve water, prevent erosion, rebuild soil nitrogen, and sustain yields with transparent accuracy (R² = 0.952, MAE ±0.388 t/ha on unseen 2009–2016 years).

3. Tools, Languages & Hardware:

TypeScript, Node.js, Python 3, React 18, Vite, MapLibre GL v5, Turf.js, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, React Query, Zod, scikit-learn, Pandas, Joblib, Vitest, Docker, Railway cloud hosting, and standard PCs.

4. Creativity:

We built a native Node.js `.joblib` inference engine inside Vite so the ML model runs alongside the React UI without needing a separate Python server.

5. Factors Considered:

prohibits back-to-back identical crops to curb pests, reports P10–P90 uncertainty with HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW data reliability flags, and keeps the interface simple and clutter-free.
